title: U.S. Justice Department Sues California Over Egg Laws That Impact, Increases Prices Nationwide - NewsBreak
text: WASHINGTON, D.C. — The U.S. Department of Justice has launched a lawsuit against the State of California, taking aim at state laws that it says are driving up egg prices across the country. The lawsuit, filed in federal court on Friday, names Governor Gavin Newsom, Attorney General Rob Bonta, and other top state officials. According to the Justice Department’s complaint, California’s laws impose strict requirements on egg and poultry farmers, including those outside the state, by banning production methods that are otherwise standard across much of the nation. Officials say these rules violate the Supremacy Clause of the U.S. Constitution and conflict with federal law. The Egg Products Inspection Act already regulates labeling and packaging for eggs and prohibits states from adding their own extra rules. In a statement shared by the Department of Justice, Attorney General Pam Bondi said, “Americans across the country have suffered the consequences of liberal policies causing massive inflation for everyday items like eggs. Under President Trump’s leadership, we will use the full extent of federal law to ensure that American families are free from oppressive regulatory burdens and restore American prosperity.” Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate also weighed in, emphasizing how California’s laws affect families in every state. “Bureaucratic red tape and unnecessary regulations implemented by the State of California have made the cost of everyday goods, like eggs, less affordable for Americans,” Shumate said. “This Department of Justice will work to free consumers from this regulatory burden and bring economic prosperity to families.”
